title: Optimal stretch for online bin stretching
formal: Determine R_stretch=limsup_{m→∞} r_m for deterministic online bin stretching, where r_m is the best stretch for exactly m bins.
definitions: For a positive integer m known to the algorithm, an adversary reveals a finite sequence of real sizes in (0,1], promised to admit an offline packing into m unit-capacity bins. A deterministic policy irrevocably assigns each item on arrival to one of exactly m labeled bins without knowledge of future items or final length. There is no running-time restriction. For a sequence σ its stretch is the maximum final load, measured in units of offline bin capacity. Define r_m as the infimum over policies of the supremum stretch over all promised sequences. No additive load term, dropped items, extra bins, or repacking is allowed. The selected large-m target is limsup_m r_m, defined as inf_M sup_{m≥M} r_m; existence of an ordinary limit is not assumed. Policies may depend on m.
answer_criterion: Supply a real number a and a complete Lean-checked proof that its absolute distance from the defined optimal ratio is at most 1/100. Certified upper and lower bounds with gap at most 1/50 qualify via their midpoint. Bounds must cover all instances and all competing policies as quantified; attaining the infimum or supremum is not required.
context: The 2024 paper improves on stretch 3/2 for sufficiently many machines. A question asking only to beat 3/2 would therefore be obsolete.
why: This measures how much extra capacity is needed when the number of bins is fixed but item order is online.

import_provenance.original_title: The optimal stretch for online bin stretching
import_provenance.original_statement: Determine the smallest worst-case stretch achievable by deterministic online packing into m bins when the entire item sequence is promised to fit offline in m unit bins. Items must be assigned irrevocably, and the central target is the optimal ratio for arbitrarily large m.
import_provenance.supplied_caveat: Remark: The 3/2 barrier was already broken before the cutoff: the cited paper gives 139/93<1.495 for sufficiently large m. The remaining question is the optimal ratio.

context_blocks.text: The 2024 paper improves on stretch 3/2 for sufficiently many machines. A question asking only to beat 3/2 would therefore be obsolete.

sentences: The input is guaranteed to fit into m unit bins offline.
Online assignments use exactly m bins and cannot be changed.
Stretch is the maximum load relative to unit offline capacity.
The selected target is the limsup of the optimal stretch as m grows.
A proof need not establish that the ordinary limit exists.
